# #3429 — notes

**Verdict: `repros`.** Still fails on `main` (`1.9.0.5433`, `ab5400907`, Debug), and on all
20 probeable release binaries from v1.4.1907 (2019-07) to v1.9.2607 (2026-07). No release we
can run has ever compiled this shader; v1.4.1907 is the oldest with a usable binary, so this
is "for as long as it is checkable" rather than "since forever".

Issue: <https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3429>, filed 2021-02-04.

## What was tested

`repro.hlsl` is a byte-faithful copy of the minimised shader in the
[2024-04-28 comment](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3429#issuecomment-2081259226)
— produced by @pow2clk from the reporter's private shader — including its blank lines and
trailing spaces, so the diagnostics land on the same line:column pairs quoted in the thread.
`cmd.txt` is the reporter's own command line, `-E main -T cs_6_0`, with no added flags: there
was no workaround in the report to inherit or question.

```
$ dxc -E main -T cs_6_0 repro.hlsl
error: validation errors

repro.hlsl:9:22: error: TGSM pointers must originate from an unambiguous TGSM global variable.
note: at '%13 = phi float addrspace(3)* [ %8, %7 ], [ %22, %11 ]' in block '#5' of function 'main'.
repro.hlsl:15:20: error: TGSM pointers must originate from an unambiguous TGSM global variable.
note: at '%15 = phi float addrspace(3)* [ %22, %19 ], [ %8, %10 ]' in block '#6' of function 'main'.
Validation failed.
[exit] 0x80004005
```

That is character-for-character the reporter's 2024 output — same two line:column pairs, same
SSA numbering — two years and eight releases later (`out-main-debug.txt`).

**Exit status is E_FAIL (0x80004005), which is an ordinary diagnosed error, not a crash.**
Every one of the 42 probes exits with exactly that status; nothing in this issue is
crash-shaped, and `internal_failure` would have been the wrong predicate.

## The defect, from source

The pointer is not ambiguous. Compiling the same source with `-Vd` succeeds and shows why
(`artifact-main-debug-Vd.ll`, generated by `make-validator-source-case.py`):

```llvm
@"\01?thingies@@3PAMA" = external addrspace(3) global [6 x float], align 4
...
  %8  = getelementptr [6 x float], [6 x float] addrspace(3)* @"\01?thingies@@3PAMA", i32 0, i32 %1
  %22 = getelementptr [6 x float], [6 x float] addrspace(3)* @"\01?thingies@@3PAMA", i32 0, i32 %17
  %13 = phi float addrspace(3)* [ %8, %7 ], [ %22, %11 ]
```

Both incoming values of both phis are GEPs into the **same** global. There is only one
`groupshared` array in the shader; no pointer in it could come from anywhere else.

`lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:3820-3849` is what rejects them. For any instruction
whose result type is a pointer in `DXIL::kTGSMAddrSpace`, it walks back through GEPs and
bitcasts looking for a `GlobalVariable` — and if the instruction is *not itself* a GEP or a
bitcast, it takes the `else` branch and emits `InstrFailToResloveTGSMPointer` without looking
at the operands at all:

```cpp
if (isa<GetElementPtrInst>(&I) || isa<BitCastInst>(&I)) {
  ...walk operand 0 through GEPs and bitcasts; error only if it does not reach a global...
} else {
  ValCtx.EmitInstrError(&I, ValidationRule::InstrFailToResloveTGSMPointer);
}
```

A `phi` is neither, so it is rejected unconditionally. So DXC's own optimizer emits DXIL that
DXC's own validator refuses — which is what makes this a compiler defect rather than a
judgement about the shader, whichever side the fix belongs on.

Corroborated a second way: `dxv.exe`, built from this repo's source, rejects the very module
`dxc -Vd` just produced, with the identical diagnostic (`manual-case-validator-source.txt`).
So this is the in-tree validator, not only the redistributable `dxil.dll` that sits beside
`dxc.exe`.

The rule's rejection of `phi` is deliberate, and the repo's own negative test says so:
`tools/clang/test/LitDXILValidation/GroupShared/tgsm-chained-gep-ambiguous.ll` — *"any other
construct (phi, select, etc.) in the middle of a chain leaves the ultimate base ambiguous and
must be rejected"*. But every ambiguous case that test constructs joins **two different**
globals (`GA` and `GB`), and it is written in hand-authored LLVM IR. It does not cover the
case here, where all the merged pointers share one base. Whether the walk should handle
`phi`/`select` whose operands all resolve to the same global, or the optimizer should not
form such a merge for TGSM in the first place, is a design call for the maintainers; the
evidence here does not settle it and the draft does not try to.

## Which optimization levels

The issue body says *"When disabling optimization it works"*. Every level was measured twice:
once by `make-optlevel-case.py` (`manual-case-optlevels.txt`) and once as a tool-made capture
with a recorded verdict, on `main-debug` (`ab5400907`). Both agree.

| flag | exit | verdict | capture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-Od` | 0 | clean | `variant-od-main-debug.txt` |
| `-O0` | 0 | clean | `variant-o0-main-debug.txt` |
| `-O1` | 0x80004005 | fails | `variant-o1-main-debug.txt` |
| `-O2` | 0x80004005 | fails | `variant-o2-main-debug.txt` |
| `-O3` | 0x80004005 | fails | `variant-o3-main-debug.txt` |
| *(none)* | 0x80004005 | fails | `out-main-debug.txt` |

`-O3` is `dxc`'s documented default (`--help`: `-O3  Optimization Level 3 (Default)`), and the
explicit `-O3` capture matches the no-flag run, so the default row is not a separate datapoint.

So the workaround is real but costs all optimization — it is not just `-O3` that trips it. Only
`-Od` and `-O0` escape.

The `-O0` disassembly shows *why*: at `-O0` the GEP is repeated inside each block
(`%14`, `%20`, `%22` all `getelementptr ... @"\01?thingies@@3PAMA"`) and the only `phi` is the
`i32` loop index. No `phi float addrspace(3)*` is ever formed, so the validator has nothing to
reject. The pointer `phi` is created by optimization, from `-O1` upward.

Worth noting for predicate design: `-O1`/`-O2` report the phis as `%11`/`%13` in blocks
`#3`/`#4`, while `-O3` reports `%13`/`%15` in blocks `#5`/`#6`. Same two source locations
(`9:22`, `15:20`), different SSA names. A predicate anchored on the instruction text would have
scored `-O1` and `-O2` as no-repro.

`-Od` also still compiles clean on the oldest and newest release binaries
(`variant-od-v1.4.1907.txt`, `variant-od-v1.9.2607.txt`), so the workaround has held for the
whole probeable history too.

## History

`bisect --linear`, all 20 bisectable releases, both predicates, no invalid probes:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `match.json` (the TGSM rule text) | **repro at all 20**, v1.4.1907 → v1.9.2607 |
| `match-compile-fails.json` (nonzero exit) | **repro at all 20** |

`--linear` rather than binary search because a validation rule can be tightened and relaxed
across releases; it was not, but the scan is what establishes that rather than assuming it.
All 42 probes exit 0x80004005.

v1.4.1907 (2019-07) is the bisection floor, so `always-repro'd` means "for as long as it is
possible to check", not "since it was filed". The report is nonetheless fully covered:
v1.5.2010 (2020-10-22) predates the 2021-02-04 filing by three months and reproduces. The
catalog's v1.5.2003 hole does not need filling here — it sits between two releases that both
reproduce, so there is no transition inside it to locate.

`always-repro'd` is a meaningful finding here rather than a build-configuration artefact: the
symptom is a diagnostic emitted by a Release-built validator, not an assert, so `NDEBUG` has
no bearing on it.

### A false transition, found and corrected

The first version of `match.json` was `contains "error: TGSM pointers must originate…"`, with
the `error: ` prefix copied from the reporter's 2024 paste. Under it, `bisect --linear`
reported **"non-monotonic history, transitions at v1.5.2010 → repro"**. That transition does
not exist. v1.4.1907 emits the same rule for the same two instructions in an older format:

```
at 0x2221ed5c658 inside block .lr.ph._crit_edge of function main TGSM pointers must originate from an unambiguous TGSM global variable.
```

— no `error: ` prefix, an instruction address and block name instead of a source line:column
and the IR text. The falsifying capture is kept verbatim in
`manual-case-predicate-correction.txt`; the predicate was loosened to the rule text alone and
every release re-probed. (The same old format appears in issue 2768's 2020 report, which is
independent confirmation that the wording changed rather than the behaviour.)

## Controls

| capture | expect | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant-od-main-debug.txt` — the reporter's `-Od` workaround | `no-match` | exit 0 |
| `variant-o0-main-debug.txt` — `-O0`, the other clean level | `no-match` | exit 0 |
| `variant-control-groupshared-main-debug.txt` — a groupshared array indexed dynamically in a loop, no merged pointer | `no-match` | exit 0 |
| `variant-control-two-globals-main-debug.txt` — an attempt at a genuinely ambiguous case | `no-match` | exit 0 |
| `variant-o1-main-debug.txt` — lowest optimization level that fails | `match` | exit 0x80004005 |
| `variant-o2-main-debug.txt` — `-O2` | `match` | exit 0x80004005 |
| `variant-o3-main-debug.txt` — `-O3`, explicit rather than implied by the default run | `match` | exit 0x80004005 |

Every row's `--expect` matches its recorded verdict. The predicate therefore does not fire on
"uses groupshared memory", nor on the same shader at a different optimization level.

The two-globals control is also a recorded **negative result**: writing to two different
groupshared arrays on opposite sides of a branch does *not* make DXC merge the pointers — it
keeps two separate stores and compiles clean. So one attempt to reach the ambiguous case from
HLSL failed, while the unambiguous case arrives from ordinary source. That is one attempt,
not a proof that no HLSL can express it.

## Compiler Explorer

<https://godbolt.org/z/61Gb43GjM> — verified by reading the shortlink back
(`api/shortlinkinfo`): four panes with the ids and arguments intended, and `repro.hlsl`'s 21
lines present verbatim. Full pane text in `manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt`.

- `dxc_1_6_2112` and `dxc_trunk` both fail with the rule.
- `dxc_trunk -Vd` compiles and shows the two `phi float addrspace(3)*` whose inputs all GEP
  `@"\01?thingies@@3PAMA"` — this is the pane that makes the bug visible rather than merely
  reproducing it.
- `hlsl_clang_trunk` compiles the same source cleanly and forms **no** merge of groupshared
  pointers at all: it keeps the address computation inside each branch. Probed with a control
  (a trivial groupshared compute shader) under identical flags, so the difference is
  attributable to the repro rather than to Clang's backend —
  `manual-case-clang-probe.txt`, which also greps both outputs for groupshared-pointer
  merges and prints a loud marker when it finds none. **Clang does not run DXC's DXIL
  validator**, so this says what Clang emits, not what the rule would accept.

The banner shifts line numbers: issue line 9 is CE line 44. Noted in the banner itself.

## Text staleness

**Not stale.** Title, body and every comment still describe what the compiler does. The
2024-04-28 comment's "still reproducible … on 1.8.2403.2" is confirmed by
`out-v1.8.2403.2.txt`, and the body's `-Od` claim is confirmed by `variant-od-main-debug.txt`.

One nuance that is *not* staleness: the body attributes the failure to
`WaveIsFirstLane` writing to a `groupshared float2` array. The minimised repro uses neither,
so the wave intrinsic is not required — but that minimisation is itself in the thread, above
nothing and contradicting nothing, and the body remains an accurate account of the reporter's
own shader. Recording it here rather than as `text_stale`, which is a claim about someone's
writing and should be held to a higher bar than this.

## Labels

Now: `bug`. Proposed add: `validation` — described in the live taxonomy as *"Related to
validation or signing"*, and this is precisely a DXIL validation rule rejecting DXIL that DXC
itself produced. Not proposing `correctness` (nothing is miscompiled — the compile fails),
nor `check-in-clang` (that label asks for a check; the check is done and recorded above), nor
any severity or effort label the evidence does not support. Recorded, never applied.

## Suggested action

`still-valid-keep-open`. The repro is minimal, public, current, and reproduces on every
release ever shipped. The remaining question is which side the fix belongs on, and that is a
maintainer decision.
